title: Sure There's a Righteous God
description: Sure There's a Righteous God in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 10 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 73, part 4, headed “The mystery of providence unfolded”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sure there's a right-eous God, Nor is re-li-gion vain, Tho' men of vice may boast a-loud, And men of grace com-plain.

lines: Tho' men of vice may boast aloud,
While haughty fools with scornful eyes
Their flesh looks full and fair,
Their wealth rolls in like flowing seas,
Free from the plagues and pains
Thro' all their life oppression reigns
Their malice blasts the good man's name,
"Is there a God that sees or hears
Till to thy house my feet were brought
Thy word with light and power
I view'd the sinners' life before,
But here I learnt their end.
And O that dreadful fiery deep
Lord, at thy feet I bow,
I call my God my portion now,
And all my powers are thine.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
